Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Mayor Elen Asatryan expressed gratitude to residents, businesses, and the community for
  their unity and cooperation during the recent wildfire emergencies. She noted that while the
  city did not experience fires, it sustained significant damage. Asatryan thanked city staff for
  their dedicated service during this unprecedented event and encouraged ongoing efforts to
  enhance preparedness. She announced that a report outlining key lessons from the wildfires
  would be presented to the council for review. The mayor also highlighted the
  disproportionate impact on the Armenian community, emphasizing the lack of
  comprehensive data to identify the needs of the community. She requested staff to draft a
  letter of support for AB-91, which aims to ensure proper representation of Armenians and
  other nationalities/ethnicities in California state forms.

  2
 Councilmembers acknowledged the hardships faced by many as a result of the fires,
expressing appreciation for city staff and volunteers who came together and worked
tirelessly during the crisis.

Councilmember Dan Brotman extended condolences to those who lost loved ones and
property. He visited an evacuation center and was reassured by the care provided to
displaced residents.

Councilmembers Brotman and Najarian jointly nominated Stefan Chraghchian to the
Planning Commission.

Councilmember Gharpetian stated that in previous years, the city has celebrated the life of
Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. However, due to the wildfire emergencies, this year’s celebration
did not take place. He encouraged everyone to count their blessings and find ways to
support communities that have lost their livelihoods. Councilmember Gharpetian asked for
an update from staff on the facilities that have been developed as a result of the 2014 bond
measure. Additionally, he urged staff to stay informed about fire incidents in neighboring
cities, including La Crescenta, Tujunga, and Sunland, to prevent potential spillover effects
into Glendale or ensure the city is prepared if they occur. He also stated that the state has
paused certain regulations to expedite rebuilding efforts and permit approvals. He raised
concerns about the environmental impact of the fires, including cleanup efforts and the
amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere. Councilmember Gharpetian
congratulated newly elected U.S. President Donald J. Trump on his victory in both the
electoral and popular votes, as well as the Republican Party for winning the Senate and
House elections. He expressed hope that all leaders would come together, regardless of
party affiliation, to fulfill their promises. Additionally, he requested reconsideration of the bike
lanes on La Crescenta Avenue.

Councilmember Najarian thanked public agencies for their continued support of Altadena
residents affected by the wildfires. He requested that the council adjourn the meeting in
honor of those who had suffered losses. Najarian also asked staff to provide a memo on the
amount of carbon dioxide released due to the Eaton Fire, so it could be compared to the
CO2 reductions achieved through Glendale’s electrification policies. He congratulated
President Trump on his election victory and, in light of the new administration's policies—
including the elimination of electric vehicle mandates, withdrawal from the Paris Agreement,
and stricter immigration enforcement—requested a report on how these changes would
impact the city.

Najarian and Mayor Asatryan nominated Ronnie Gharibian to the CDBG Commission.

Councilmember Kassakhian congratulated President Trump on his reelection and expressed
gratitude to outgoing officials for their service to the country. He called for prayers for the
success of leaders in Washington, D.C., and California.
Councilmember Kassakhian encouraged the public to use the My Glendale App to report
downed trees or hanging wires and urged staff to replace any U.S. flags on public property
that were damaged or worn out.

City Manager Roubik Golanian, Director of Public Works Daniel Hernandez, and Deputy Fire
Chief Jeff Brooks provided a recap of the windstorm events and the response efforts carried
out in the city. Golanian expressed his deepest appreciation to staff who worked tirelessly in
the Emergency Operations Center and in support roles throughout the city.
